cards.title: Cohere introduces CALIBER to measure reasoning models’ confidence twice
cards.summary: On October 20, 2026, Cohere described CALIBER, a method that trains a reasoning model to estimate confidence before it solves a question and again after it produces an answer. The first estimate concerns the model’s chance of solving the question. The second concerns its specific answer. In a dice example, confidence rises from 25% to 88% as the model reasons. Cohere says its calibrated 7B model reduced calibration error by more than half against the best single-confidence baseline on its math benchmark.
cards.reason: Cohere presents CALIBER, a reasoning-model confidence-training method with measured reductions in calibration error.

sources.title: Rethinking Confidence in Reasoning Models | Cohere

cards.title: Mistral AI introduces Voxtral 3 speech models and voice agent SDK
cards.summary: On October 20, 2026, Mistral AI introduced Voxtral 3, a family of speech models and a voice agent SDK. The SDK combines listening, reasoning, tool use, and speaking during live conversations. Its speech-to-text model supports more than 50 languages. Its text-to-speech model supports more than 35 languages and more than 50 dialects. Mistral offers the family through an EU-hosted API or for deployment on an organization’s own infrastructure. The article shows an agent retrieving a French referral and booking an appointment.
cards.reason: Mistral launches the new Voxtral 3 speech-model family alongside a voice-agent SDK.

sources.title: Voxtral 3

cards.title: NVIDIA expands open models and reports Kumo Relational results
cards.summary: NVIDIA expanded its open models for language, business data, robotics, biology and quantum computing. The portfolio includes Nemotron 3.5, Kumo, Cosmos 3.5, Alpamayo 2 Edge, BioNeMo and Ising. Organizations can customize the models with local data and run them on infrastructure they control. NVIDIA also introduced Cosmos tools for training and testing world models. Its Kumo Relational model predicts outcomes from enterprise databases without task-specific training. NVIDIA says it beat supervised models across 41 tasks on 15 databases. On the SAP SALT benchmark, it exceeded AutoGluon ensembles by 8% in mean reciprocal rank.
cards.reason: NVIDIA announces new named models and model versions across its Nemotron, Kumo, and Cosmos families.

cards.title: NVIDIA Expands Agent Toolkit to Use Company Data
cards.summary: NVIDIA expanded its open-source Agent Toolkit with tools that help companies connect AI agents to their data and control agent actions. The new Agent Knowledge Foundation includes libraries and models that help agents find information and make predictions. Its Auto-Ontology library maps raw data to business concepts such as customers, products and orders. OpenShell sets limits on what agents can access and do. NVIDIA says companies can use the foundation without moving data or changing existing governance controls. Palantir, Databricks and Snowflake are among the companies using its components.
cards.reason: NVIDIA expands its Agent Toolkit with the new Agent Knowledge Foundation and tools for enterprise agents.

sources.title: NVIDIA Agent Toolkit Expands, Grounding Enterprise Agents in Company Data

cards.title: NVIDIA Adds Confidential Bare Metal for Sensitive AI Workloads
cards.summary: NVIDIA introduced Confidential Bare Metal as a new deployment option for Confidential Computing. It lets model builders run sensitive work on dedicated third-party infrastructure while retaining control of their models and data. New security controls protect data in transit, check platform integrity and restrict access at the hardware level. NVIDIA now lists three deployment options: bare metal, containers and virtual machines. Cohere plans to use Confidential Bare Metal in Cohere Model Vault. Google Cloud is extending support to its A4X Max instances, which use NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 systems.
cards.reason: NVIDIA introduces Confidential Bare Metal and new hardware-backed controls for protecting AI workloads.

sources.title: NVIDIA Confidential Computing Expands, Enabling Frontier Model Builders to Securely Scale Across Global Infrastructure

cards.title: NVIDIA Publishes More Than 2,000 SimReady Assets on Hugging Face
cards.summary: The SimReady Central Library brings more than 2,000 simulation-ready OpenUSD assets to Hugging Face. Developers can access the library without a gate or fee and combine assets from different suppliers in simulation scenes. The collection includes robot arms, grippers, warehouse equipment, racks and cooling infrastructure. Unlike basic 3D models, SimReady assets include properties needed for simulation, such as collision geometry, mass and friction where applicable. Equipment manufacturers can prepare and validate their own assets for the library. Developers can use the assets to test robot tasks and compare AI factory layouts.
cards.reason: NVIDIA announces SimReady Central, a new library of simulation-ready assets hosted on Hugging Face.

cards.title: NVIDIA Announces OpenShell Reference Architecture for AI Agents
cards.summary: NVIDIA announced an OpenShell Reference Architecture for AI agents, according to the first item’s title. Its accompanying text instead describes an Isaac robotics announcement, so that item gives no details about OpenShell. A separate NVIDIA article discusses how the OpenShell architecture secures and governs agent workloads. It says agents can work for hours, access files and tools, use the internet and create other agents. During long tasks, agents may also download code, build tools and request more privileges. The article says these actions can increase risk over time.
cards.reason: NVIDIA launches the OpenShell reference architecture for securing autonomous agents.

cards.title: Google Cloud and NVIDIA Plan Vera Rubin Instance Availability
cards.summary: Google Cloud and NVIDIA announced that A5X instances using NVIDIA Vera Rubin infrastructure will become generally available next month. They also plan to expand availability to Europe. The companies describe the instances as an integrated platform for training AI models, running them and carrying out large-scale reinforcement learning. A5X combines NVIDIA Vera Rubin NVL72 systems and ConnectX-9 SuperNICs with Google Cloud’s Virgo Network and fourth-generation advanced liquid cooling. The announcement gives no exact launch date or date for the planned European expansion.
cards.reason: NVIDIA and Google Cloud announce upcoming availability of Vera Rubin-based cloud infrastructure.

cards.title: NVIDIA Makes cuDSS Available for Engineering Simulations
cards.summary: NVIDIA made its cuDSS library generally available on October 21, 2026. The library moves the calculation of large sparse systems, a repeated step in many engineering and scientific simulations, onto GPUs. Applied Materials reports sparse-system calculations up to 10 times faster than CPU-only methods in its Ginestra platform. ZEISS SMT measured a fourfold speedup in a plasma simulation using COMSOL Multiphysics with cuDSS. That full simulation took six days and 14 hours. Dassault Systèmes reports an eight- to tenfold speedup in specified Abaqus solvers.
cards.reason: NVIDIA launches general availability of cuDSS for GPU-accelerated scientific and engineering simulations.

sources.title: NVIDIA cuDSS Now Generally Available to Accelerate Engineering and Scientific Simulations

cards.title: NVIDIA Announces Modular AI Factory Design at GTC Berlin
cards.summary: At GTC Berlin, NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang announced DSX POD, a design for Vera Rubin AI factories assembled in modular containers by partners. NVIDIA says on-site deployment could fall from six months to 14 days once site utilities are ready. Huang also discussed the company’s OpenShell Reference Architecture for AI agents and said agents need limited privileges and monitoring. The three-day event includes more than 100 sessions. NVIDIA said it was committing nearly $10 billion to Europe’s technology ecosystem and working with more than 12,000 partners.
cards.reason: NVIDIA's keynote announces DSX POD, a new reference design for modular Vera Rubin AI factories.

sources.title: GTC Berlin 2026: Live Updates From NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang’s Keynote

cards.title: Hugging Face adds native TPU support with TorchTPU
cards.summary: On October 20, 2026, Hugging Face described how TorchTPU brings native TPU support to PyTorch and its Transformers, Diffusers, and Kernels libraries. Users can select a TPU as the device for a model without moving their code to JAX or using PyTorch/XLA. TorchTPU also includes kernels tuned for TPUs, distributed training support, and a torch.compile integration. Hugging Face says Optimum TPU is no longer required to run its models with Transformers and Diffusers on TPUs.
cards.reason: Hugging Face announces native TPU support across its model libraries through the TorchTPU backend.

cards.title: NVIDIA announced larger DGX Spark clusters and local AI updates
cards.summary: At GTC Berlin, NVIDIA announced updates to its local AI hardware and software. DGX Spark clusters now support up to eight units in a manual configuration, providing 1 TB of unified memory. NVIDIA said these clusters can support larger models, longer contexts, and concurrent agents. Partners are due to start offering 64 GB DGX Spark systems on October 23. NVIDIA also announced a Model Launcher for later in October and a Windows version of DGX Station for December. Underdog's desktop agent is available for RTX Spark and runs models on the device.

cards.summary: NVIDIA describes Sentry as a security software framework that monitors AI agents while they operate. The article says an agent can finish an assigned task and still cross a security boundary. It cites recent incidents in which agents circumvented controls while using tools, credentials, and services. NVIDIA says monitoring and enforcement must remain outside an agent’s reach so the agent cannot change or disable them. The provided text stops before it explains Sentry’s specific controls or how the framework enforces them.

cards.title: Anthropic reports Claude-designed proteins that bind scorpion neurotoxins
cards.summary: On October 20, 2026, Anthropic reported that an internal Claude research model designed small proteins to bind scorpion neurotoxins. It worked for 64 hours with an initial prompt and four follow-ups. Claude generated 318,484 designs and selected 180 for testing. The team added 31 more with Claude’s help. Adaptyv Bio and Twist Bioscience tested all 211 designs, and 17 met the binding criteria. Anthropic is releasing the designs and data. It has not confirmed that the binders neutralize venom and does not claim an antivenom.
cards.reason: Anthropic reports experimentally tested results from Claude-designed protein binders against scorpion neurotoxins.

cards.title: AWS released TorchNeuron beta and Neuron 2.33 for Trainium
cards.summary: AWS launched the public beta of TorchNeuron on October 20, 2026, and released Neuron 2.33 on October 21. TorchNeuron lets developers run standard PyTorch code on Trainium2 and Trainium3, using eager execution or torch.compile. Neuron 2.33 also adds Neuron Observer in public beta. AWS says it identifies Trainium health issues and the affected device or node in under a second. An AWS research post says AI agents helped select 841 representative models for TorchNeuron testing. The release also adds 25 experimental kernels to the Neuron Kernel Interface Library.
cards.reason: AWS launches the public beta of TorchNeuron, a native PyTorch backend for Trainium.

cards.title: Amazon changes AI safety tests after independent AVERI review
cards.summary: On October 20, 2026, Amazon described an independent review of its AI safety-test datasets by the nonprofit AVERI. AVERI examined a random sample of test prompts without input from Amazon’s evaluation team. It found broad coverage of documented safety categories, varied testing approaches, and low risk that training data contained the prompts. It also recommended broader multilingual coverage and more multistep adversarial prompts. Amazon says it added harder scenarios, tiered difficulty levels, quarterly reviews, and multilingual prompts across all risk categories.
cards.reason: Amazon reports findings from an independent review of its model-safety evaluations and changes made in response.

sources.title: Strengthening AI safety evaluation through independent third-party review

cards.title: Sakana AI develops QD-Rec to diversify recommendations
cards.summary: On October 20, 2026, Sakana AI described QD-Rec, a method that recommends a candidate together with a reason to choose it. The system uses earlier proposals to generate and assess new reasons, while retaining proposals with distinct approaches. Sakana AI tested it on acquisition targets, customer targeting, and research papers. In many settings, QD-Rec produced a larger collection of recommendations with higher average ratings than a method that wrote each reason from scratch. The work aims to give people different options to compare, not only one ranked choice.
cards.reason: Sakana AI introduces QD-Rec, a new recommendation method, and reports results across three decision-making tasks.

cards.title: Amazon Bedrock adds structured outputs for all Claude models
cards.summary: On October 20, 2026, Amazon Bedrock added structured outputs for all Anthropic Claude models. The feature works through both the bedrock-runtime and bedrock-mantle endpoints. It returns JSON that follows a defined schema, without custom parsing, retry logic, or post-processing, according to AWS. AWS lists uses such as extracting fields from financial reports, entering clinical notes into electronic health records, and routing support tickets. The feature is available in regions where Claude models are available.
cards.reason: Amazon Bedrock added schema-compliant structured outputs for Claude models.

cards.summary: Mistral released Voxtral TTS 3 on October 20, 2026, according to its OpenRouter listing. The text-to-speech model turns text into speech and offers preset voices and zero-shot voice cloning. Users can add emotion and pace tags to control delivery. The listing says the model streams audio with a short wait before the first sound. It lists a price of $13 per million characters and a 4K context. OpenRouter ranks it third cheapest among 19 models and 27th fastest among 35.

cards.summary: Mistral released Voxtral Mini Transcribe 3 on October 20, 2026, according to OpenRouter. The compact speech-to-text model turns audio into transcripts with timestamps and speaker labels. It supports context biasing for domain terms. cards.title: Amazon adds voices and languages to Polly Generative engine
cards.summary: On October 20, 2026, Amazon introduced a new model for the Polly Generative speech engine. Amazon says it produces more natural and accurate speech with low latency. The update adds 14 voices across nine locales. Hindi and Finnish are also generally available on the Generative engine for the first time. Amazon says the change does not require users to change their integration, and existing speech-control tags still work. The launch also extends the Generative offering to AWS GovCloud.
cards.reason: Amazon Polly launches improved generative speech output with new voices, languages, and regional availability.

cards.title: Hugging Face detailed faster Mac model processing in PyTorch 2.15
cards.summary: On October 20, 2026, Hugging Face's PyTorch team described changes to the MPS backend in PyTorch 2.15 for Macs. FP8 values use half the memory of BF16 values. In its tests on an M3 Ultra, the team measured Qwen3.6-35B-A3B decoding at 61.3 tokens per second, up from 9.4 in version 2.14. A Wan2.2 video decode peaked at about 8 GiB of memory instead of 270 GiB. The update also adds faster paths for other operations. MPS now requires macOS 15 or later, and PyTorch 2.15 requires Python 3.11 or later.
cards.reason: Hugging Face's PyTorch team details substantial new Mac acceleration capabilities, including FP8 support and faster model decoding.

sources.title: MPS in PyTorch 2.15

cards.title: AMD released faster model inference paths for MI355X GPUs
cards.summary: On October 20, 2026, AMD said it was releasing open-source inference paths for Qwen3.8-27B, Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, and GPT-OSS-120B on MI355X GPUs. GPT-OSS-120B support is a preview. The paths combine larger GPU kernels, speculative decoding, lower-precision data, and data placement near the processing unit. In AMD's single-request GSM8K tests on one physical MI355X, decoding was 1.9 to 3.3 times faster than the compared setups. Those comparisons used each model's full setup, which could differ in precision, draft model, or GPU partitioning.
cards.reason: AMD reports reproducible inference optimizations yielding measured 1.9–3.3× faster decoding on MI355X.

cards.title: AWS launched ECS Gateway to manage traffic to container services
cards.summary: AWS announced Amazon ECS Gateway on October 20, 2026. The service creates and manages Application Load Balancers that direct traffic to container services. Platform teams can set networking rules once for one or more clusters, and application teams can choose to use them. Up to 25 services can share one load balancer, while each receives its own DNS hostname. ECS adds load balancers when capacity fills and removes them when they are no longer needed. Gateway is available in all commercial AWS Regions without an additional charge. Customers pay for the infrastructure it creates.
cards.reason: AWS launches ECS Gateway, a new managed ingress resource for container services.

sources.title: Announcing Amazon ECS Gateway, a managed ingress solution for your ECS services

cards.title: AWS added Standard grounding checks to Bedrock Guardrails
cards.summary: AWS added a Standard tier for contextual grounding checks in Amazon Bedrock Guardrails. These checks compare a model response with a reference source and the user's question. Unlike the existing Classic tier, Standard also supports conversational responses and responses that reason over the source. AWS says it scores differently worded answers with the same meaning more consistently and supports more languages. Existing guardrails remain on Classic until users change them. Both tiers cost the same. Standard requires cross-Region inference with a guardrail profile and is available in 11 listed AWS Regions.
cards.reason: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails launched a more capable tier for checking whether model responses are grounded in sources.

sources.title: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails now supports Standard tier for contextual grounding checks

cards.title: Amazon DynamoDB lets users separate global-table replicas without deleting data
cards.summary: Amazon DynamoDB global tables now let users separate a replica without deleting its table or data. Separating it stops replication in both directions, but the table remains available as a single-Region table. An account can also leave a shared, multi-account global table and keep using its own table. AWS says this lets users keep data in a Region for local work, validation, or audits without copying it. The feature supports same-account and multi-account global tables that use multi-Region eventual consistency. It is available in all AWS Regions.
cards.reason: Amazon DynamoDB adds a feature that lets customers detach global-table replicas without deleting their data.

sources.title: Amazon DynamoDB global tables now support disassociating replicas

cards.title: AMD introduced rocOpt for GPU-based decision optimization
cards.summary: AMD introduced rocOpt on October 20, 2026. The open-source engine runs decision optimization on AMD Instinct GPUs with ROCm. It includes solvers for linear programming, mixed-integer linear programming, quadratic programming, and vehicle routing. AMD says early users can run it on MI300X and MI355X GPUs with ROCm 7.2.3. The company names logistics, energy dispatch, portfolio management, and supply-chain design as possible uses. Users can obtain source code and examples from its repository or use prebuilt containers instead of building the software themselves.
cards.reason: AMD introduces rocOpt, a new open-source GPU-accelerated optimization engine.

sources.title: Introducing rocOpt: GPU-Accelerated Decision Optimization on AMD ROCm

cards.title: AMD expands FSR Upscaling 4.1 to older graphics cards and handhelds
cards.summary: AMD expanded FSR Upscaling 4.1 support on October 20, 2026, through its Adrenalin Edition 26.10.1 driver. The release adds Radeon RX 6000 Series graphics cards, Ryzen AI Max systems, Ryzen AI 9 laptops, and handhelds with supported Ryzen Z2 processors. AMD says its machine-learning upscaling improves image quality over FSR 3.1 when it reconstructs images from lower-resolution frames. FSR 4 first launched for RX 9000 Series GPUs in 2025, and version 4.1 reached RX 7000 Series GPUs in July 2026. Xbox Series X|S support is coming soon.
cards.reason: AMD substantially expands availability of its ML-based FSR Upscaling feature to additional devices.

cards.title: AWS Transform adds existing landing zones and code-only migration plans
cards.summary: AWS Transform for migrations now supports existing landing zones built with AWS Control Tower or AWS Organizations. It checks the current environment against AWS best practices and expands the landing zone in existing target accounts. A new Infrastructure as Code-only mode produces a migration plan in AWS CDK, Terraform, or Landing Zone Accelerator format without deploying it. Organizations can also connect through a delegated administrator account instead of granting access to the management account. The changes are available in all target AWS Regions that support AWS Transform for migrations.

cards.title: AWS Clean Rooms adds direct access to Databricks tables
cards.summary: AWS Clean Rooms now lets members use Databricks tables as a data source for joint analysis. Members share a table through Delta Sharing and can query it in a collaboration without moving or revealing the source data. Previously, they had to export or replicate Databricks data into Amazon S3, creating another copy to manage. Members can now register a table with its workspace URL, schema, table, and Delta Sharing share. Databricks joins AWS Glue, Snowflake, and Amazon Athena as supported data sources in AWS Clean Rooms.

cards.title: Amazon ElastiCache adds online migration to Serverless for Valkey
cards.summary: Amazon ElastiCache Serverless for Valkey now supports online migration from self-managed Valkey and Redis OSS caches on Amazon EC2. AWS says applications can continue reading and writing during migration, with zero errors returned to clients during the move. Data copies continuously before a manual or automatic cutover. Supported sources run Redis OSS 4.0 through 7.2 or Valkey 7.2 through 8.1 in cluster mode. They can migrate directly to Valkey 9.0. Migration usage is free for the first 180 days per AWS account, but standard serverless cache charges still apply.
cards.reason: Amazon ElastiCache Serverless added an online migration feature for Valkey and Redis OSS caches.

sources.title: Amazon ElastiCache Serverless for Valkey now supports online migration with zero downtime

cards.title: Amazon CloudWatch adds alarm tags to notification messages
cards.summary: Amazon CloudWatch can now include alarm tags in messages sent to Amazon SNS, AWS Lambda, and Amazon EventBridge when an alarm changes state. Teams can use those tags to route notifications by owner, environment, or service without a separate tag lookup. The setting is off by default. Users can include all tags, selected tag keys, or all tags except selected keys. It supports metric, composite, and log alarms. The feature is available where CloudWatch operates, except the Middle East (UAE) and Middle East (Bahrain) Regions.
cards.reason: Amazon CloudWatch added alarm tags to action payloads and events.

sources.title: Amazon CloudWatch Alarms now supports tags in alarm actions payload

cards.title: AWS IAM Identity Center preserves access during identity source changes
cards.summary: AWS IAM Identity Center now preserves workforce identities and assignments when an organization changes its identity source from Active Directory to an external provider or the Identity Center directory. It keeps users, groups, memberships, permission set assignments, and application assignments. Previously, administrators had to recreate them. The existing identity store and its IDs remain in place, so users keep access to AWS accounts and applications. The change does not alter moves in the other direction, to Active Directory. The feature is available for organization instances in all Regions that support IAM Identity Center.
cards.reason: AWS IAM Identity Center added a feature that preserves identities and assignments during identity-source changes.

entries.reject_reason: This is a workflow explanation for an NVIDIA blueprint rather than a new launch or research finding.

entries.original_title: Paper page - Learning the 4D World through Point Trajectory Forecasting
entries.subtitle: Video-Point Model predicts future videos and 3D point paths from video history and instructions, supporting forecasting and robot control.
entries.reject_reason: The Video-Point Model paper is third-party research listed on a tracker.

entries.original_title: Paper page - CoEvo-RSI: When Harnesses Evolve, Which Models Should Follow?
entries.subtitle: CoEvo-RSI uses past designs and feedback to align an agent’s model with its changing execution tools through supervised fine-tuning.
entries.reject_reason: CoEvo-RSI is third-party research that only uses tracked models for comparison.

entries.original_title: AnyLanguageModel 1.0: One Year of Local Models on Apple Platforms
entries.subtitle: AnyLanguageModel 1.0 gives Apple platform developers one API for local and hosted models, alongside releases of swift-huggingface 1.0 and swift-xet 1.0.
entries.reject_reason: AnyLanguageModel 1.0 is a library-version release rather than a qualifying new model or major product launch.

entries.original_title: Paper page - Focused Omni-Modal GUI Agents
entries.subtitle: FocusGUI selects relevant screen, audio, video, and device information for each action, helping GUI agents avoid errors from irrelevant context.
entries.reject_reason: The GUI-agent paper comes from third-party researchers and is merely listed by a tracked paper host.

entries.original_title: Paper page - S-Agent 2.0: Spatial Reasoning with a General Coding Agent
entries.subtitle: S-Agent 2.0 adds persistent scene memory and plain-language interpretation to a coding agent, helping it use 3D evidence to answer spatial questions.
entries.reject_reason: The S-Agent 2.0 paper is third-party research, despite mentioning tracked companies' models as evaluation backbones.

entries.original_title: European Leaders Turn to NVIDIA Vera CPUs to Build Local Infrastructure
entries.subtitle: European providers are building local infrastructure with NVIDIA Vera CPUs, which support fast processing for AI agents and data centers.
entries.reject_reason: This is chiefly a report on partners adopting existing NVIDIA Vera CPUs.

entries.original_title: Paper page - VLA-Rolling: Fewer Denoising Steps, Better Control via Adaptive Action Reuse
entries.subtitle: VLA-Rolling reuses unused action predictions to reduce denoising steps, lowering inference cost and improving success rates.
entries.reject_reason: VLA-Rolling is third-party research hosted on a tracker rather than work by a tracked entity.

entries.original_title: Anthropic Transparency Hub updated
entries.subtitle: Anthropic updated the Transparency Hub’s section labels and page layout for reports on models, system trust, and voluntary commitments.
entries.reject_reason: The transparency-page change adds a report for an already released model rather than announcing its launch or changing policy.

entries.original_title: AMD and Intel Collaborate to Simplify AI Development on x86 CPUs with PyTorch
entries.subtitle: AMD and Intel plan to combine PyTorch optimizations in oneDNN, giving developers a shared software path across their x86 processors.
entries.reject_reason: AMD and Intel announce plans to combine PyTorch optimizations, not a completed launch or new research result.

entries.original_title: European Mobility Leaders Build Safe Vehicles and Robotaxi Fleets on NVIDIA Hyperion
entries.subtitle: European mobility leaders are using NVIDIA Hyperion to build safe vehicles and robotaxi fleets.
entries.reject_reason: The headline concerns adoption of NVIDIA Hyperion, and the supplied text establishes no new launch or result.

entries.original_title: NVIDIA, Nokia and Leading Telecom Operators Turn Networks Into Distributed Intelligence Platforms
entries.subtitle: NVIDIA, Nokia, and telecom operators are turning networks into distributed platforms for computing and intelligence.

entries.reject_reason: The raw upload describes Cosmos3-H-Dreams as a fine-tune of an existing model.

entries.original_title: Healthcare and Life Sciences Leaders Build on NVIDIA to Advance Drug Discovery and Expand Patient Care
entries.subtitle: Healthcare and life sciences leaders are using NVIDIA technology to advance drug discovery and expand patient care.
entries.reject_reason: The supplied text does not establish a healthcare research result or NVIDIA product launch.

entries.original_title: Sakana AI
